statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 5 of 100 in the low band, twenty points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the price path this score measures. Stress is 60 in the elevated band on an unresolved Saudi pipeline outage, crude near 100 dollars and a Wednesday policy decision priced for an increase. Confidence is 87 on a complete verified closing set.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD, and the single shared reading applies to each instrument. Two independent facts support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, yet finished 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, while NQ futures traded down to 29,040.50 after the inflation print and recovered to settle 29,391.75, a 459-point round trip that retraced rather than extended. Second, CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, which is 23 hours after this horizon ends, so all twenty-four forecast slots describe a closed market in which a persistent no-retracement path cannot form. No evidence-based danger window is published, because a halted contract offers no interval to mark. Stress remains elevated and is the honest carrier of weekend exposure: the Saudi East-West pipeline that bypasses Hormuz is shut after drone strikes, WTI sits at 99.99 dollars after a 9.7% weekly advance, the ten-year yield finished just below 5%, and the 16 September decision carries a market-implied probability near 87% of a 25 basis point increase. That exposure reprices into a single Sunday opening print rather than into an intraday path, which is gap risk rather than the path risk Tail scores.
headline: A shut tape into the weekend: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44 and 0.91% higher but mid-range, NQ retraced a 459-point round trip after hot core CPI, VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84, and an unresolved Saudi pipeline outage travels into a Sunday reopen that lies beyond this window.
body: Friday's price path is complete and it granted retracement. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close. The cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished 105 points below the high and 55 above the low, so the closing auction neither extended the advance nor broke it. NQ futures were wider and more instructive: a 29,040.50 low after the 12:30 UTC inflation print gave way to a 29,499.50 high and a 29,391.75 final tick, a round trip of roughly 459 points in which mean reversion worked in both directions. VIX fell 2.00 points or 11.21% to 15.84, closing near the low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range, and the advance was broad rather than narrow, with all eleven S&P 500 sectors and every Magnificent Seven megacap higher while Nvidia and Micron lagged marginally. The macro backdrop is the source of the elevated Stress. August CPI rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year, core rose 0.3% against a 0.2% consensus, and the CPI energy index gained 2.1% on the month and 16.3% on the year. Preliminary September Michigan sentiment fell to 47.8 from 51.7 with year-ahead inflation expectations at 4.6%. The latest H.15 observation shows the two-year at 4.56%, the ten-year at 4.95% and the thirty-year at 5.37%. Crude eased 2.43% to 99.99 dollars and Brent 2.98% to 104.42 dollars on news that Iran would meet Gulf states in Oman about the Strait of Hormuz, but WTI still gained 9.7% on the week and Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, roughly seven million barrels a day of Hormuz-bypass capacity, remains shut after drone strikes. None of that exposure can reprice inside this horizon. CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so every one of the twenty-four forecast slots covers a market with no venue, no auction and no price path. Tail therefore holds a thin residual floor that represents deferred gap exposure, while Stress carries the energy and policy risk and Confidence decays only as the verified closing set ages.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 00:00 UTC to 23:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at Tail 13 in mixed mode and eases to 11 through the Asian session, then firms into a trend-up read between 06:00 and 11:00 UTC as European hours extended the advance, with Tail between 13 and 15. The 12:30 UTC inflation release marks the only departure from the low band: the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC slots were published at Tail 21 and 22 in event/whipsaw mode, mapping to WATCH and a yellow status, with Confidence cut to 70 and 80 while the two-way reaction resolved. From 14:00 UTC the assessment returned to the low band in mixed mode near Tail 15 to 17, and the final four slots step downsharply to 13, 7, 6 and 6 in normal mode as the cash close passed and the futures halt removed the price path. Stress declined almost monotonically across the window, from 86 at the open to 62 at the close, while Confidence held between 87 and 89 outside the event hours.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, 23 hours after this horizon ends. Conditional Tail opens at 5 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, holds that residual floor through the overnight and Saturday European hours, and steps to 6 from 13:00 UTC, 7 from 19:00 UTC and 8 in the final slot as the stock of unpriced weekend information grows toward a reopen that still lies beyond the window. The maximum forecast value of 8 remains seventeen points below the 25-point block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON and green in all twenty-four slots and no danger window is published. Stress traces a shallow valley, easing from 60 to 58 through the dead hours as Friday's realized volatility decays, then rebuilding to 64 by the end of the window as attention shifts to Monday's Hormuz meeting in Oman and to a Wednesday policy decision priced near 87% for an increase. Confidence decays from 87 to 79, which tracks the ageing of a complete verified closing set rather than any deterioration in conditions, since no fresh observation is obtainable before the reopen. Dominant mode is normal throughout: a closed market has no directional structure to classify.
